[Lähde: BBC World | URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cevmdxz4872o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss]
Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attack as manhunt continues

One woman has been killed and at least 29 others injured after a van was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night, in what officials say was likely an "Islamist terror attack".

Police have launched an intensive manhunt for the suspect in the German capital.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has condemned the incident as a "heinous" attack.

The attack happened at about 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT). A report was made to police in Berlin that a white vehicle had been driven into crowds at a Pride event in the capital.

Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered at Tiergarten park, near the iconic Brandenburg Gate, for the annual event, which is known as Christopher Street Day.

Some people were also stabbed in the incident, with a blade officials believe could have been a machete.

Shortly afterwards, the Pride event was cancelled.

A performance was abruptly brought to a end, with organisers taking to the stage and advising the crowd to start walking towards the exits.

As the message was being given to the crowd, the word "evacuation" was projected onto a large screen on the stage.

Unverified video posted to social media showed large crowds of people leaving the scene as emergency vehicles raced to the scene.

At about 01:00 local time, police confirmed that one woman had been killed and many more had suffered injuries.

A short time later, police confirmed they had found the vehicle believed to have been used in the attack, saying it had crashed into a tree.

At about 03:30, police said on X they had identified a suspect with Islamist links. No arrest has been made or motive suggested.

The search area was widened to the entire city and involved thousands of police, including officers from surrounding German states.

On Sunday, police officers stood guard outside an apartment block in Berlin's Tiergarten district, which is said to be the suspect's home.

The suspect has been named by police as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese background.

He was known to police and has committed a number of crimes, officials said. He had previously been sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison, but the sentence was commuted to parole.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the suspect had been radicalised.

German media outlets are reporting he is a supporter of Islamic State group (IS), and tried in the past - unsuccessfully - to join the organisation

[Lähde: CBS News | URL: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/berlin-lgbtq-pride-christopher-street-attack-ramming-suspect-search-germany/]
The car ramming attack on a Berlin LGBTQ+ Pride parade on Saturday is believed to have been motivated by Islamist extremist ideology, authorities said on Sunday, as a search for the suspect continues. The attack at one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ events left one dead and at least 29 injured.

German police have identified the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. Police described him as being part of Berlin's "Islamist scene" and someone who is known to authorities.

"Everything we see here points to us dealing with an Islamic terror attack," Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Sunday.

Dobrindt said that Ballout was born in Germany and that his mother was naturalized in 2002, three years before he was born. He said the suspect had been convicted in Berlin in the past, though he didn't specify for what. He said that he had been given a suspended sentence of 1 year and 10 months.

Police searched an apartment in Berlin's Schöneberg district early Sunday, but said they found no one there. The suspect's heavily damaged vehicle remained at the site of the attack on Sunday morning.

In a wanted notice issued Sunday, police warned that Ballout may be armed and dangerous and said the public should avoid "direct contact."

Authorities are also working to determine if he acted alone. Investigators believe that one or more people may have left the vehicle after it came to a stop. Some victims also suffered stab wounds, raising the possibility that others were involved in the attack, but authorities have not confirmed that. Dobrindt said the suspect is believed to have injured people with a machete.

Berlin's fire service said that of the injured, three have life-threatening injuries, eight were seriously injured, and five had slight injuries. Police have not identified the deceased victim.

Before the attack, huge crowds had spent hours celebrating peacefully. The event, in front of Berlin's iconic Brandenburg Gate, featured dozens of floats, live music and a march.

"It's a dark day for the community," said Julian Miethig, who had attended the event and been planning to go to an afterparty when he heard that "something bad happened" at the parade.

The attack is the latest in a series that have left the country grappling with questions about public safety.

payload.title: Yksi kuoli Berliinin Pride-tapahtumaan tehdyssä ajoneuvoiskussa – epäiltyä etsitään
payload.summary: Pakettiauto ajettiin väkijoukkoon Berliinin Pride-tapahtumassa lauantai-iltana. Yksi nainen kuoli, vähintään 29 ihmistä loukkaantui ja poliisi etsii 21-vuotiasta epäiltyä.
payload.content:
Yksi nainen on kuollut ja vähintään 29 ihmistä loukkaantunut, kun pakettiauto ajettiin lauantai-iltana väkijoukkoon Berliinin Pride-tapahtuman yhteydessä. Saksan viranomaiset pitävät tekoa alustavasti islamistisena terrori-iskuna. Poliisi etsii 21-vuotiasta miestä ja varoittaa, että epäilty saattaa olla aseistautunut ja vaarallinen.

Ajoneuvo ajettiin juhlaväen keskelle

Hyökkäys tapahtui noin kello 22 paikallista aikaa, eli kello 20 GMT, Tiergartenin puiston tuntumassa lähellä Brandenburgin porttia. Berliinin vuosittaiseen Christopher Street Day -tapahtumaan oli kokoontunut satojatuhansia ihmisiä. Tapahtuma kuuluu Euroopan suurimpiin seksuaali- ja sukupuolivähemmistöjen Pride-juhliin.

Poliisille tehtiin ilmoitus valkoisesta ajoneuvosta, joka oli ajettu väkijoukkoon. Ajoneuvoa on kuvattu pakettiautoksi. Viranomaisten mukaan yksi tai useampi henkilö poistui siitä törmäyksen jälkeen. Poliisi ja syyttäjät kertoivat myös, että useita ihmisiä oli ilmeisesti puukotettu. Puukotuksia koskeva tieto on esitetty alustavana.

Poliisi etsii 21-vuotiasta epäiltyä

Poliisi ja syyttäjät ovat julkaisseet etsintäkuulutuksen 21-vuotiaasta Abdul Balloutista ja pyytäneet yleisöltä apua hänen löytämisekseen. Sunnuntaina annetussa tiedotteessa ihmisiä kehotettiin välttämään suoraa kontaktia epäiltyyn, koska tämä saattaa olla aseistautunut ja vaarallinen. Berliinissä on käynnissä laaja etsintäoperaatio.

Balloutin epäillään vahingoittaneen useita ihmisiä liikkuvalla ajoneuvolla myöhään lauantai-iltana. Poliisi on kuvannut häntä Berliinin islamistiseen ympäristöön kuuluvaksi ja viranomaisten ennestään tuntemaksi henkilöksi. Epäillyn etsintä jatkuu Saksan pääkaupungissa.

Viranomaiset tutkivat mahdollista terrori-iskua

Saksan sisäministeri Alexander Dobrindt sanoi sunnuntaina, että alustavat havainnot viittaavat islamistiseen terrori-iskuun. Hänen mukaansa kaikki tähän mennessä saadut tiedot tukevat tätä arviota. Viranomaiset epäilevät teon motiivin liittyvän islamistiseen ääriajatteluun, mutta kyse on yhä kesken olevan tutkinnan alustavasta arviosta.

Liittokansleri Friedrich Merz tuomitsi tapahtuneen julmaksi hyökkäykseksi. Sunnuntaina surevia ihmisiä kokoontui Brandenburgin portille kunnioittamaan uhrien muistoa. Kokoontuminen oli lähellä Tiergartenin puistoa, jossa Pride-juhla järjestettiin. Samalla poliisi jatkoi epäillyn etsintää ja pyysi yleisöä noudattamaan varoitusta, ettei häntä lähestytä.
summary_bullets: Yksi nainen kuoli ja vähintään 29 ihmistä loukkaantui ajoneuvoiskussa.
Poliisi etsii 21-vuotiasta Abdul Balloutia ja varoittaa lähestymästä häntä.
Saksan viranomaiset arvioivat alustavasti, että kyseessä oli islamistinen terrori-isku.
payload.journalist_note: Terrorismiin ja epäillyn motiiviin liittyvät luonnehdinnat ovat Saksan viranomaisten alustavia arvioita. Epäillyn etsintä ja tapahtumien kulun selvittäminen jatkuvat.

Viranomaiset epäilevät teon motiivin liittyvän islamistiseen ääriajatteluun, mutta kyse on yhä kesken olevan tutkinnan alustavasta arviosta.

Liittokansleri Friedrich Merz tuomitsi tapahtuneen julmaksi hyökkäykseksi. Sunnuntaina surevia ihmisiä kokoontui Brandenburgin portille kunnioittamaan uhrien muistoa. Kokoontuminen oli lähellä Tiergartenin puistoa, jossa Pride-juhla järjestettiin. Samalla poliisi jatkoi epäillyn etsintää ja pyysi yleisöä noudattamaan varoitusta, ettei häntä lähestytä.

Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attack as manhunt continues One woman has been killed and at least 29 others injured after a van was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night, in what officials say was likely an "Islamist terror attack". Police have launched an intensive manhunt for the suspect in the German capital. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has condemned the incident as a "heinous" attack. The attack happened at about 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT). A report was made to police in Berlin that a white vehicle had been driven into crowds at a Pride event in the capital. Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered at Tiergarten park, near the iconic Brandenburg Gate, for the annual event, which is known as Christopher Street Day.

A police manhunt is under way after a suspect rammed a car into a crowd at a Pride event in the German capital on Saturday night.

German authorities have issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van ramming near Berlin's Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 25 others. Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. They said he is believed to have injured several people with a moving vehicle late Saturday evening, and that one or more people apparently then left that vehicle. Several people were also apparently stabbed, they added. Sunday's notice warned the public to avoid "direct contact" with the suspect, saying that he may be armed and dangerous. Germany’s Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said initial findings suggest "we have experienced an Islamist terror attack". Mourners have gathered at Brandenburg Gate in central Berlin to pay their respects to the victims of yesterday's attack.

The car ramming attack on a Berlin LGBTQ+ Pride parade on Saturday is believed to have been motivated by Islamist extremist ideology, authorities said on Sunday, as a search for the suspect continues. The attack at one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ events left one dead and at least 29 injured. German police have identified the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. Police described him as being part of Berlin's "Islamist scene" and someone who is known to authorities. "Everything we see here points to us dealing with an Islamic terror attack," Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Sunday.
